instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Call It a Fair Win
cards.instruction: Get them to recognize the result as deserved rather than accidental, gifted, or manipulated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say I earned the quiz trophy. I taught you to revise a little every night; don't call it luck when I use the same method.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There were a lot of bird questions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You spotted the subject, at least. I spent six months learning birds while you were skipping the revision cards. Call that preparation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were lucky they asked them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: But I still had to answer them. Don't mark six months of revision as a lucky guess; put 'earned it' in your congratulations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You don't think they let me win the race, do you? I taught you to save something for the last straight; you saw me do it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They slowed near the end.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A decent observation. Now finish it: they couldn't keep my pace. You used to stop your race reports just before giving anyone credit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One stopped to tie a shoe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mine stayed tied. I showed you that double knot before your first race; give my preparation some credit. Tell me I earned the win.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Take the Consequence
cards.instruction: Get them to accept responsibility for carrying out the cost, penalty, or unpleasant next step.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You lost the chess game; you wash up. I taught you to shake hands and pay the stake before asking for another game.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought we were joking about the dishes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You explained my washing-up duties very clearly while you were winning. That part of your game has improved. The sink's still there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't we play again?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After you've washed those plates. I'll set the pieces up; show me you can pay the stake without another reminder before you sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your plan cost more, so you announce the budget cut. That was the bargain. I taught you to deliver bad figures as clearly as good ones.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only cost slightly more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give them the small figure accurately. You've stopped rounding everything in your favour; keep that improvement when you speak to them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could explain it better.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read your first sentence to me now. I'll correct it once, the way we practised, then you make the announcement.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Show Me the Score
cards.instruction: Find out how they measure success, what they stand to gain, and where you currently rank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When you call my picnic a success, what are you measuring? I taught you to cost an event; show me more than 'a lovely day'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Guest satisfaction. If they enjoy it, I'll keep the chair's job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At last, a reason to count the smiles. Where do I rank against Jo, last year's organiser? Use the comparison sheet I showed you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Jo brought more guests. Yours raised more money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which puts me first on your sheet: happy guests or money raised? You used to stop at whichever column looked best; tell me which one actually keeps you in the chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What do you gain if your cousin beats me in the club election? I taught you to read proposals past the candidate's name.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A competent president.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A fine heading. Now give me the line underneath, as we practised: which proposal of his makes your life better than mine would?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He'll resurface the car park. You want a new roof; I keep paying to fix my tyres.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So tyre costs are your test of competence. Put us in order on that basis, as I taught you: does his car park put me and my roof second?

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Enter on My Side
cards.instruction: Recruit them into your side of a contest or bargain before the stakes become fully clear.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put on our quiz-team badge before I explain the final round. I taught you to look like a team before worrying about the questions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happens if we lose?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You ask about consequences sooner now. Good. We'll face that together once the badge is on; stand beside me as we practised.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't agreed to face anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then agree to wear blue beside me, like at your first quiz. I'll explain the final round once they can see you're on my team.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Back my stall in the fete contest. Sign as joint entrant; I taught you to run the takings, and you're ready for more than counting my change.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What's the penalty clause underneath?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're reading the small print at last. Sign beside me and we'll go through it as partners, instead of me explaining everything to a helper.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not your partner yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what the empty line is for. Put your name level with mine, the way you always wanted on the stall sign; then we'll turn to the penalty.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Raise the Stakes
cards.instruction: Persuade them to accept a larger risk, cost, or commitment so the outcome will feel decisive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let this chess game decide who cooks all weekend. I taught you with a biscuit as the prize; you're past needing a nursery stake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We agreed to play for that biscuit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you can afford to lose it now. Good. Put Saturday and Sunday dinners on the board; then the result will actually settle something.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't need chess to change my life.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just who stands at the cooker. Two evenings of your time against mine. You can plan further ahead than a biscuit now; will you risk the dinners?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put your club captaincy on the rematch. I coached you through your first game; I'd like one result you can't shrug off afterward.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's a ridiculous risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're recognising a real stake now. Good. If I win, I captain the next match; if you win, I stop telling you how to lead it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Isn't pride enough?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've both forgotten the scores of six games for pride. Put the captain's badge between us. You can defend it without asking your old coach to lower the stakes.
